claims.claim: Hong Kong should tighten rent control on subdivided units but not with a hard cap on initial rents.
A light initial-rent band combined with tenure security and faster rehousing is the better-targeted package.
A hard cap would likely harm the households it is meant to protect.
SDU tenants pay a 15–25 percent per-square-foot premium over mainstream flats.
Real rent burden worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income even under the 2021 ordinance.
The 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance capped increases within existing tenancies but left initial rents untouched and excluded co-living SDUs.
The status quo is a slow transfer from the poorest renters to small landlords.
Long-run supply elasticity for marginal SDU-type stock is estimated at 0.31–0.48.
A 15 percent cut in initial rents would transfer about HK$900 per month to incumbents while pricing out 3,000–4,000 households per year.
Berlin's experience shows that after the Mietendeckel fell, new-contract rents jumped above the pre-cap trend line.
Stable SDU stock under the 2021 ordinance is not evidence that a binding cap is safe.
First-generation controls show consistent contraction, while second-generation controls show small or null effects.
The 2021 ordinance is second-generation and non-binding at the first-rent margin, which is why stock held steady.
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year.
A band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing 40–60 staff-years to build.
The subcommittee's modelling could not identify any enforcement design protecting the newest-arrival tail first rather than last.
An NGO survey of 440 households found 61 percent would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year tenure security and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer.
A published, indexed per-square-foot band framed as rate-capping avoids the compensation and judicial-review risk of a hard cap.
A band plus tenure security will not deliver the full HK$800 monthly relief Mr Chan imagines.
Rent control treats the price symptom of a quantity problem.

cites.sentence: SDU tenants pay a 15–25 percent per-square-foot premium over mainstream flats [D1p1], and real rent burden has worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income even under the 2021 ordinance [D2p2].
SDU tenants pay a 15–25 percent per-square-foot premium over mainstream flats [D1p1], and real rent burden has worsened from 31 to 34 percent of income even under the 2021 ordinance [D2p2].
The 2021 Tenancy Control Ordinance capped increases within existing tenancies but left initial rents untouched and excluded co-living SDUs [D1p3].
Mrs Wong's experience — nine years in an SDU, no written agreement, rent raised "by whatever the market of desperate newcomers bears" [D4p1]

The academic literature estimates long-run supply elasticity for marginal SDU-type stock at 0.31–0.48, meaning a 10 percent cap-induced rent cut removes roughly 3–5 percent of stock over five years [D6p1].

The modelled Hong Kong scenario is stark: a 15 percent cut in initial rents transfers about HK$900 per month to incumbents while pricing out 3,000–4,000 households per year, mostly new arrivals and newly formed households [D6p4].
Those excluded are precisely the population named in [D1p2]
Berlin confirms the mechanism: after the Mietendeckel fell, suppressed increases released and new-contract rents jumped above the pre-cap trend line [D7p2].
Crucially, the stable SDU stock under the 2021 ordinance [D2p1]

The working paper distinguishes first-generation controls (hard caps on levels), which show consistent contraction, from second-generation controls (caps on increases), which show small or null effects [D6p2].

The 2021 ordinance is second-generation and non-binding at the first-rent margin — which is exactly why stock held steady, and why the think-tank argument that "capacity exists for more control" [D12p2]
Inspection capacity covers under 6 percent of stock per year, and a band-based initial-rent cap would require a certifiable tenancy register costing 40–60 staff-years to build [D10p1].
The subcommittee's own modelling concedes it could not identify any enforcement design under which the newest-arrival tail is protected first rather than last [D10p3].
Mrs Wong's landlord never gave her a written agreement [D4p1]; tenants least able to complain are exactly those a cap is meant to help.
The NGO survey of 440 households found 61 percent would trade a nominal rent increase for three-year tenure security, and 74 percent for a faster public-housing offer [D11p1].
Mr Chan, asked what would help most, did not name rent — he named the waiting list [D3p3].

The legal opinion offers a defensible middle instrument: cap initial rent by reference to a published, indexed per-square-foot band, framed as rate-capping rather than confiscation, which avoids the compensation and judicial-review risk of a hard cap [D9p2].
This is also the direction the government appears to be moving, with a "floor-standard + rent band" package rather than a hard cap [D12p1].

The honest trade-off is this: a band plus tenure security will not deliver the full HK$800 monthly relief Mr Chan imagines [D3p2], and it will not satisfy those who see landlord margins as the problem.
But it avoids the contraction arithmetic of [D6p4], it targets the insecurity tenants actually name [D11p1], and it preserves the stock that houses someone tonight.
But it avoids the contraction arithmetic of [D6p4], it targets the insecurity tenants actually name [D11p1], and it preserves the stock that houses someone tonight.
Rent control treats the price symptom of a quantity problem [D11p2].
